Architecture Diagram

The application is a server-rendered catalog management site with optional Azure integrations. Its primary request path is a browser, MVC controller, catalog service, and either SQL Server or an in-memory mock catalog.

Data Storage & External Services

The application stores catalog items, brands, and types in SQL Server through Entity Framework, or serves mutable in-memory catalog data when mock mode is enabled. Image storage can use local mock behavior or Azure Blob Storage; Azure Active Directory and Application Insights are optional integrations. The Compose configuration also defines a SQL Server container.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects mock or SQL-backed catalog behavior from configuration and registers request-scoped services.
  • The MVC application owns catalog persistence; there is no separate catalog API or gateway service.
  • Image storage and Azure AD integrations are optional and selected through configuration flags.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem is a mutable MVC form model and EF entity used for catalog create and edit requests and catalog responses. CatalogBrand and CatalogType provide catalog lookup data. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the catalog-list response model. The image-upload action returns an anonymous JSON object containing an image name and URL. No separate gateway DTOs, immutable records, protobuf schema, GraphQL schema, or OpenAPI document was identified; JSON output uses the MVC/System.Web serialization path.

Communication Patterns

  • Browser-to-application requests use synchronous HTTP and server-rendered MVC views; the image upload returns JSON.
  • Controllers call ICatalogService and IImageService directly. The SQL-backed catalog service uses Entity Framework and CatalogDBContext; there is no inter-service REST or message-broker workflow.
  • Optional image operations use Azure Blob Storage; the SQL connection can use a configured connection string or an Azure managed identity token.
  • Azure AD OpenID Connect and cookie authentication can be enabled by configuration. When disabled, custom middleware assigns an application identity to each request; catalog write actions carry [Authorize].
  • No service discovery, API gateway, retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, or asynchronous messaging mechanism was identified.
  • Compose maps the MVC container to HTTP on port 80 and does not configure TLS. The application does not declare a transport-security policy in the selected deployment files.
  • The app container declares a dependency on SQL Server, but the main Compose file does not wait for the SQL health check before startup.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. SQL Server container starts before the MVC container according to depends_on.
  2. The SQL health check uses sqlcmd in the Compose override, but the application dependency does not wait on a healthy condition.
  3. MVC Application_Start registers dependencies and routes, initializes SQL schema/seed data when mock mode is off, initializes image storage, and configures telemetry.
  4. Azure Blob Storage, Azure AD, and Application Insights are external services and are not started by Compose.

Secrets Provisioning Workflow

Web.config enables Environment, Azure Key Vault, and Secrets configuration builders. CatalogConfiguration reads application settings, and the optional Key Vault builder tolerates initialization failures when configured as optional. SQL can use a connection string or an Azure managed identity token provider when UseAzureManagedIdentity is enabled. Compose supplies external variable references for storage, telemetry, and Azure AD; no deployment identity/RBAC provisioning workflow is defined in this subdirectory. The Compose development override also contains a hard-coded SQL Server SA password.

Core Business Workflows

The application lets catalog administrators browse and maintain the products, brands, and categories presented by the eShop catalog. It supports optional image upload and storage, while purchasing, checkout, and customer-order workflows are outside this application.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct offered in the catalog, including price, stock thresholds, and image referenceBelongs to one brand and one type
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementBrand classification for catalog itemsCan be associated with many items
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementCategory/type classification for catalog itemsCan be associated with many items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server, optional Azure Blob Storage, optional Azure AD

Catalog persistence has a single source of truth in this application. Mock mode replaces SQL-backed catalog operations with an in-memory list; no cross-context entity ownership or service API exchange was identified.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog list or a product detail page.
  2. CatalogController requests paginated items or one item from ICatalogService.
  3. In SQL mode, CatalogService queries CatalogDBContext and includes the brand/type relations; in mock mode, CatalogServiceMock reads the in-memory catalog.
  4. The controller adds image URLs and renders the Razor view.

Workflow 2: Create or Edit a Catalog Item

  1. An authorized administrator opens the create or edit form; the controller supplies available brands and types.
  2. The browser can upload an image through POST /uploadimage. PicController accepts only content decoded as JPEG, PNG, or GIF, then the image service stages it and returns a temporary reference.
  3. The administrator submits the catalog form. MVC model validation checks the submitted CatalogItem.
  4. The catalog service creates or updates the item. SQL mode allocates an item ID from a SQL sequence and saves through EF6; mock mode mutates its in-memory list.
  5. If a temporary image reference is present, the image service moves the staged image to the item location. The controller redirects to the catalog.

Workflow 3: Delete a Catalog Item

  1. An authorized administrator requests the confirmation page for an item.
  2. The controller loads the item and renders the confirmation view.
  3. On POST, DeleteConfirmed loads and removes the item through the catalog service, then redirects to the catalog.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no independently deployed business services or gateway aggregation flows. The MVC application directly reads and writes its catalog data in SQL Server and optionally calls Azure Blob Storage for image operations. When image storage is unavailable or disabled, the selected image service implementation controls the fallback behavior; no retry or circuit-breaker policy was identified. Database updates and blob operations are separate, non-atomic actions.

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • CatalogItem.Name is required. Price must be between 0 and 1,000,000 and match the configured decimal format with at most two fractional digits.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock threshold must each be between 0 and 10,000,000. EF mapping requires an item to reference an existing brand and type.
  • The database mapping limits item name to 50 characters and brand/type labels to 100 characters. OnReorder is a boolean domain indicator; no explicit item lifecycle state machine was identified.
  • Item identifiers are allocated from the catalog HiLo SQL sequence in SQL mode. The in-memory mock service assigns the next ID from the current maximum.
  • Catalog write actions use [Authorize]; Azure AD cookie/OpenID Connect authentication is optional. When AAD is disabled, the application installs custom middleware that assigns a claims identity.
  • EF persistence uses individual SaveChanges operations. Image storage is performed separately from database persistence, so these changes do not share an atomic transaction.
  • Account and catalog actions emit log4net informational messages; the authentication failure notification redirects but does not log the failure event.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and ASP.NET MVC 5.2.7, with several older integration packages. The package set includes beta configuration-builder packages and legacy System.* support libraries; moving to a newer .NET runtime will require compatibility review rather than only changing a target framework.

Notable Observations

  • The project uses classic packages.config, and its 146 entries include framework support and transitive packages as well as application-facing libraries.
  • The ASP.NET Redis session provider and Redis client are present, but no active Redis session configuration was found.
  • Messaging and blob libraries are declared although the app's primary business path is catalog management.
  • The selected solution contains no separate test project or test-scoped package set.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application models a catalog of items, brands, and types and uses Entity Framework 6 over SQL Server when mock mode is disabled. A mock service provides in-memory catalog behavior for development and demonstration.

Caching Strategy

No active application data cache was identified. ASP.NET output caching is globally configured with a zero-second duration and NoStore=true; session uses the framework default in-process behavior. Redis session-state packages are declared but no active Redis provider configuration was found.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The MVC application is the sole owner of the catalog tables and accesses SQL Server directly through EF6. There are no separate service databases, cross-service queries, CQRS read models, or service-to-service aggregation patterns. Image files are optionally stored in an Azure Blob Storage container; this is separate from catalog relational data. The mock implementation keeps catalog state in an in-memory list.
